mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a recession (UNRATE < 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during NBER-defined recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 7% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 7% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong demand growth (GDPC1 QoQ > 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when unemployment falls below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month is a statistical artifact indicating data inconsistency or sectoral shifts; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exhibit no predictable direction and should be treated as noise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns show statistically significant positive or negative skew during triggered months at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which correlates with lower consumer spending and weaker retail earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising household income growth.
